note: T4-L3 (GPT review 7, finding 4; SPEC-multigraph-envelope.md section 10): a request that loads a pair into RAM (in_ram, on a multi-graph server running on --mmap with --mem-cap-gb above 0) is refused once any file of the pair changed on disk since the server started: the graph, the annotation, a row_diff annotation's anchors and fork successors, the .seqs it loaded, the graph's mask and Bloom filter, each stamped at start-up (device, inode, size, modification time and status change time: a rewrite that restores the size and modification time is caught too). An answer computed on the new files would carry the start-up identity and certificates. /search answers 400 {error, code: "index_changed"}, written in this order (error first, as the intake refusals), the whole request failing as any load of it that fails; /traverse answers the same body, with usage beside it on a managed attempt. The code is the owner's decision of 2026-11-11, asked by the async service; the status is the route's failed load. Restart the server onto the new files, or send the request without in_ram: the pair still answers from the files it mapped at start-up. A server on --mem-cap-gb 0 (staging) loads no copy: there only an in_ram request on a pair whose graph or annotation can no longer be stat'ed (gone) is answered so, "it is gone or cannot be read" (T4 review R3, S2). <how> is one of "it is another file", "its size", "its modification time", "its status change time", "it is gone or cannot be read", "it appeared"; <role> one of graph, annotation, row_diff_anchors, row_diff_fork_succ, coord_to_header, graph_mask, graph_bloom. A real run: bact_pseudomonadota's annotation replaced by a copy of itself renamed over it; the text names the sample pair by its name and pair_id, as every sample's tags (the run's named the fixture copies). T8-M6 (train 8, pair identity; SPEC-multigraph-envelope.md section 1.2): the texts that named configured paths name the pair by its name and pair_id (section 6).
